summary: Ranking functions number rows in an order you choose, and differ in how they handle ties.
points: ROW_NUMBER gives every row a different number, even when tied.
RANK gives ties the same number, then skips: 1, 1, 3.
DENSE_RANK gives ties the same number without gaps: 1, 1, 2.
Top N per group means ranking with PARTITION BY, then filtering in an outer query.

example.sql:
SELECT name, salary,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS row_num,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rnk,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS dense
FROM employees;
example.explanation: Ben and Chloe tie on salary, so the three columns show the difference clearly.
